title: quell-prefetch-thrashing-triggered-by-maintenance-windows-across-hosting-modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Escalation from multiple customers (SafeBank on Private, two enterprise tenants on Dedicated, and sporadic Hosted alerts) reporting periodic spikes in tail latency for very long context requests. Spikes correlate with maintenance/upgrade windows and autoscaler/cordon events. Symptoms: sudden drop in short-request throughput, queue amplification, and a multi-second tail for long-sequence requests leading to customer SLA breaches.
background: Over the last 10 days we've seen 3 escalations: a regulated customer on Private observed hour-long degradation during an agent upgrade window; two Dedicated customers saw recurring 99.9th percentile spikes shortly after node maintenance; Hosted platforms showed transient bursts tied to autoscaler churn. Initial triage points to interaction between continuous prefetch/prefetch-quarantine logic, admission windows, and host-level maintenance states (cordon/drain). This causes prefetch eviction oscillation and admission reservoir collapse under mixed-length workloads.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a mixed-length synthetic workload with 80% short (<=128 tokens) and 20% long (>=8192 tokens) requests at a sustained arrival rate matching customer production.
2) Trigger a node maintenance scenario: cordon + rolling drain of 10-20% of serving workers (simulate kernel-level restart or upgrade).
3) Observe scheduler admission behavior and continuous prefetch eviction logs; monitor inflight-window occupancy and KV cache churn.
4) Reproduce across hosting modes by toggling Private cluster maintenance scripts, Dedicated pool scale-down, and Hosted autoscaler simulated transient failures.
observed_behavior: Short requests are squeezed out of admission after maintenance begins; the scheduler over-prefetches long contexts, leading to eviction thrash of KV entries and starvation of short flows. Batches grow in latency and KV cache miss rates spike. Telemetry shows correlated increases in batch formation time and a drop in successful early-dequeue counts.
root_cause: Race between maintenance-triggered evacuation (cordon/drain) and continuous prefetching plus an admission reservoir that lacks urgency bias for short requests. The prefetch logic aggressively holds long-context slots without backpressure, causing eviction thrash when worker availability changes. Scheduler heuristics don't differentiate maintenance-induced capacity shrink from normal load variation, so admission windows widen incorrectly and allow long contexts to dominate.
mitigation_and_hotfix: hotfix-1: Add immediate maintenance mode flag to scheduler that temporarily reduces prefetch budget and enforces short-request priority (backported to runtime-2.4.1). Deployed as emergency rollout to Private customer cluster and Dedicated pools.
hotfix-2: Short-term admission cap: limit in-flight long-context count to a fixed percentage during node transitions to keep short-request velocity stable.
hotfix-3: KV eviction hysteresis: increase grace period before evicting KV entries during maintenance windows to reduce thrash.
hotfix-4: Quick dashboard and alert rule to detect maintenance-induced admission skew (new SLO guardrail).
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): Deploy hotfix-1 and hotfix-2 to a single Dedicated pool with synthetic traffic and one Private customer staging cluster. Validate 99th/99.9th latency improvements for short flows.
Phase B: Expand to remaining Dedicated pools during off-peak; schedule Private customer production upgrade with customer's ops team (SafeBank) after signoff.
Phase C: Push configuration to Hosted control plane as a feature flag that auto-triggers maintenance mode when autoscaler announces drain events.
Fallback: Revert feature flag and restore previous admission caps if tail regressions or throughput regressions observed beyond threshold.
testing_plan: Unit tests: scheduler maintenance-mode gate and admission bias logic (added coverage for mixed-length patterns).
Integration: end-to-end soak with mixed-length workload generator and simulated cordon/drain events for 48 hours across all hosting modes.
Perf regression: benchmark token throughput and 99.9th latencies pre/post with production-like traffic; target <10% throughput loss while restoring tail latency for short requests.
Chaos tests: run node kill and network partition experiments to ensure maintenance-mode triggers correctly and doesn't mask unrelated faults.
monitoring_signals: alert: maintenance-admission-skew (fires when short_request_velocity drops >60% during cordon/drain events)
customer_communications: 2026-03-11: Initial incident reply sent to SafeBank account team acknowledging investigation and workaround (temporary reduced long-context concurrency).
2026-03-12: Follow-up with Dedicated customers including scheduled maintenance window to apply hotfix-1 canary.
2026-03-15: Drafted post-deployment summary and SLA remediation plan pending PM/legal review.
followups: Permanent fix: rework admission reservoir to be maintenance-aware and include adaptive urgency for short flows (roadmap item, estimate 13 pts).
Evaluate if autoscaler signals can be extended in Hosted to proactively trigger maintenance-mode earlier to reduce impact.
Add long-context throttling knobs in customer-facing API for regulated/private deployments to let customers opt into conservative concurrency during upgrades.
Schedule postmortem meeting 2026-03-18 and produce blameless write-up and action items.
dependencies: ENG-70233 (deterministic-replay-canary) - use canary harness for stepwise rollout
PM-412 (customer-notifications) - coordinate SLA language and credits
DES-88 (console-alert-ux) - UX for maintenance-mode alerting in Console
blockers: Awaiting on-call infra permission to perform Private customer canary upgrade (safebank-ops signoff). Also need legal signoff on SLA remediation text before wide customer comms.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on cross-hosting behavior. Implementation must be conservative for Hosted (feature-flag first) and coordinated closely with Customer Success for Private deployments. Keep rollback steps ready and instrument telemetry to measure regressions within 10 minutes of rollout.
